Ein Längenphonem wird nicht aufgestellt. 7.1.3.2 Ton Alle Textbeispiele sind tonal bezeichnet. Dabei werden Hochton mit (´), Steigton mit (ˇ) und Fallton mit (ˆ) markiert, Tiefton bleibt unbezeichnet. Eine systematische Tonologie kann noch nicht gegeben werden, jedoch ist deutlich, daß tonale Unterschiede kaum eine lexikalische, aber eine stärkere grammatische Bedeutung haben. new_statements.translation: 7.1.3 Prosodic phenomena. 7.1.3.1 Length. What needs to be said about phonemically significant length in consonants (plosives) and in vowels has been said above. No length phoneme is set up. 7.1.3.2 Tone. All text examples are tone-marked. High tone is marked with (´), rising tone with (ˇ) and falling tone with (ˆ); low tone is left unmarked. A systematic tonology cannot yet be given, but it is clear that tonal differences have hardly any lexical, but a stronger grammatical, significance. This will become clear in the presentation of nominal and verbal inflection.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No word-stress rule is stated. Rottland's joint phonology of the six Datooga dialects (including D6 Bianjida) recognises only two prosodic phenomena, length and tone (high, rising, falling vs. unmarked low); tone is mainly grammatical. Stress (Druckakzent) is not mentioned for Datooga at all, whereas the same book's Kalenjin chapter has a 'Länge, Druckakzent, Ton' section, so the omission looks deliberate. The only weak-syllable remark is that short vowels in final position of polysyllabic words are realised very weakly and strongly centralised (p. 155).
new_statements.exceptions: None; the author states that a systematic tonology cannot yet be given.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonology stated jointly for all Datooga dialects (D1-D6) from Rottland's own 1970s fieldwork; the Bianjida (D6) material was obtained from an informant outside the Bianjida home area (note 17, p. 29). Tone marked in text examples; no citation-form vs. phrase distinction drawn. The second-hand summary of Rottland 1983: 220 (SUGIA 2001 snippet) agrees: 'Datooga is a tone language.. low tone (unmarked), high tone and a falling tone.. no systematic analysis'.
new_statements.identity_note: bian1249 Biyanjiida = Bianjida (/bía:njí:da/), Rottland's Western Datooga dialect D6 (Heine 1982 report and JALL 1985 snippets: 'Bianjida D 6'); Glottolog places it as a sister of North-Central Datooga (dato1239 Barabayiiga-Gisamjanga, bura1273 Buraadiga, isim1234 Isimjeega-Rootigaanga). Glottolog's alternative names 'Rotigeenga/Rotigenga' conflict with Rottland, for whom Rotigenga is D4 (Glottolog root1238 under isim1234); Klose 2001 gives the synonyms Bianjiida, Bianjit, Bijanjida, Utatu. No source describes Bianjida on its own: the quoted statement is Rottland's joint phonology of all six Datooga dialects, into which his D6 data (collected from a Bianjida informant outside the home area, p. 29 n. 17) enter. Struck 1911's accent rule used for dato1239 concerns the Mangati/Barabaig dialect and is not transferred here.

sources.note: The chapter is explicitly joint for all six Datooga dialects (p. 153 'Das folgende Inventar gilt für alle Datooga-Dialekte'; p. 155 'Für alle Datooga-Dialekte..'), D6 = Bianjida. §7.1.3 'Prosodische Erscheinungen' (p. 155) has only 7.1.3.1 Länge (no length phoneme set up) and 7.1.3.2 Ton (high, rising, falling marked, low unmarked; no systematic tonology yet; tone has little lexical but stronger grammatical function). sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 28: Bianjida (/bía:njí:da/) is the southernmost Datooga group, around Itigi, heavily Bantuised (Nyamwezi as L2); note 17 p. 29: the Bianjida are the only Datooga group from whom Rottland obtained information and language material only outside their home area. The morphology pages cite D6 (Bianjida) forms throughout (e.g. p. 184 devoicing in D6, the passage Kießling 2000 cites for 'the Bianjida dialect'), confirming D6 = Bianjida and that Bianjida data underlie the joint description. TOC confirms §7.1.3 = 'Prosodische Erscheinungen: 1. Länge 2. Ton'.
